newsitem.title: USA: KDP puts a buy on perilous Marvel debt.
newsitem.headline: KDP puts a buy on perilous Marvel debt.

text.p: KDP Investment Advisors Inc said it has issued a buy recommendation on the debt of Marvel Entertainment's holding companies in the aftermath of Tuesday's 25 to 30 point slide.

Marvel shares and debt sank on Tuesday after Andrews Group Inc offered to buy 80.1 percent of new Marvel common stock for $350 million, well below market cost. The acquisition would be paid for in cash and/or Toy Biz Inc common stock, Andrews said.
The deal would dilute current shares which back the outstanding Marvel debt.

Phelps Hoyt, vice president of KDP's fixed-income research group, said prospects for a better offer from controlling shareholder Ronald Perelman or another entity would lift the share price from current levels, thereby adding value to the stock-secured debt. Furthermore, Hoyt even values Marvel shares higher under a bankruptcy than under Perelman's plan.
Andrews Group and other entities controlled by Perelman now own 80 percent of Marvel's equity.

"Perelman is going to argue you're better off with him versus a bankruptcy, but I think it's the opposite," Hoyt said. "Rather than handing the store over to Perelman today and lose 80 percent of the investment, I would rather take the chance of going through bankruptcy and keeping shares undiluted."

Under Perelman's offer, Hoyt values the Marvel stock at $1.70 per share. A better offer would only boost that level, he said, adding that even under bankruptcy the shares could be valued around $4.00.

Marvel Holdings Inc's "old" bonds and Marvel (Parent) Holdings Inc's "new" bonds were marginally lower on Wednesday, according to distressed debt traders. The old bonds were quoted at 17 bid, 18 offer and the new bonds were quoted at 14-1/2 bid, 16 offer.
The old and new bonds traded around 46 and 40 on Friday, respectively, traders said.
Marvel shares were quoted down 1/8 on Wednesday afternoon to 2-5/8 after a 1-7/8 point drop on Tuesday.
Hoyt said Marvel's independent board of directors, which has a fiduciary duty to minority shareholders, should consider alternatives to Perelman's "outrageous" plan."
"The stable of characters associated with the X-men, Spiderman and various other things they have may be worth something to somebody," he said.
Marvel Entertainment reported a third-quarter loss of $0.12 per share which resulted in a failure to satisfy certain financial covenants contained in its credit agreements.
The company is seeking waivers of the covenants and a restructuring of credit agreements.
